intent: An earned node that becomes WRONG has an invalidation path. Contradiction is the fifth tenure behavior alongside crossing honesty, provenance append, promotion, and lazy decay. Invalidation marks a node at read time (invalidate-don't-delete), preserving history ('what did we believe when' stays answerable). A contradicting deposit lands as a new node with a provenance link to what it contradicts, and the contradicted node's standing drops to a state that excludes it from resolution walks without destroying it.
why: The field survey's sharpest finding: production failures are dominated by stale/contradicted/wrongly-retained facts, NOT recall failures — yet benchmarks test recall only. Measured: 97.8% of 10,134 Mem0 entries junk after 32 days; benchmark-91.6% collapsing to ~49% effective at 38% staleness (arXiv 2606.15903). The tenure loop handles corroboration and neglect but not wrongness — a node promoted to 'earned' that later becomes false has no downward path except waiting 14 days for decay, and decay exempts corroborated nodes. The lived symptom: the librarian confidently repeats something that was true last week.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) a contradicted earned node still appears in resolution walks at its former standing; (2) the contradicting deposit does not record WHAT it contradicts (no provenance link); (3) the invalidated node is deleted rather than marked (history lost); (4) invalidation fires on structure alone (cosine similarity) without an inference step confirming actual contradiction — near-topic is not contradiction; (5) a self-contradicting deposit within the same crossing invalidates itself (same-crossing honesty still holds).
design_notes: Cite Zep/Graphiti bi-temporal model: event time + ingestion time, valid_from/valid_to/invalid_at on edges; contradiction INVALIDATES, never deletes. Fits our decay's existing shape (invalidate-at-read, history preserved). Open questions: (a) does contradiction detection happen at deposit time (LLM judges incoming vs standing) or at walk time (discovered during resolution)? Deposit-time is the field's best-performing but costs ~2.3s/case. (b) What standing state does an invalidated node get — a new state 'invalidated', or does it drop to 'hypothesis' with a flag? (c) Can an invalidated node be RE-validated by later evidence? Probably yes — invalidation is a tenure event, not a deletion.
borrow_cite: Zep/Graphiti bi-temporal model (event time + ingestion time; valid_from/valid_to/invalid_at — contradiction invalidates edges, never deletes, history preserved). CURATOR forgetting-improves-accuracy (arXiv 2606.25115): net-value-per-byte pruning, accuracy ROSE where stale memory corrupted answers. Mechanism re-authored; the temporal-invalidation IDEA and the accuracy-through-forgetting EVIDENCE are borrowed.
out_of_bounds: Proactive notification of invalidation to past sessions (that's ticket #1's mechanism extended). Consolidation and warm set (tickets #3, #4). Any change to the promotion or decay physics beyond adding the fifth behavior.
